questions.solution: (a) Ni in $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}$ exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. Cl is a weak field ligand (high spin). It will not cause pairing of electrons. Hence, configuration of $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{Cl})_4\right]^{2-}$ is Tetrahedral with two unpaired electrons (i.e., paramagnetic) and has $s p^3$ hybridisation. (b) In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3\right]^{3-},\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4\right)_3^{2-}$ is a bidentate ligand thus, give octahedral structure. (c) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$, Ni exist as $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ ion. $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$is a strong field ligand (low spin). Causes pairing of electrons of $3 d$ orbital. Hence, the structure of is square planar and it is diamagnetic. (d) In $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4\right]$, Ni has zero oxidation state. i.e., CO is a strong field ligand causes rearrangement and pairing of electrons of $3 d$ and $4 s$ orbital. Structure of $\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{CO}_4\right)$ is tetrahedral with $s p^3$ hybridisation and it is diamagnetic. Hence, (4) is the correct answer.

questions.solution: Given that, $f(x)=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$ For injective: Let $x_1, x_2 \in \boldsymbol{R}$ such that $f\left(x_1\right)=f\left(x_2\right)\Rightarrow \frac{x_1}{\sqrt{1+x_1^2}}=\frac{x_2}{\sqrt{1+x_2^2}} \Rightarrow \frac{x_1^2}{1+x_1^2}=\frac{x_2^2}{1+x_2^2}\Rightarrow x_1^2+x_1^2 x_2^2=x_2^2+x_1^2 x_2^2 \Rightarrow x_1^2=x_2^2\Rightarrow x_1=x_2$ So, $f(x)$ is injective. For surjective: Let $y=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\Rightarrow y^2\left(1+x^2\right)=x^2 \Rightarrow y^2+y^2 x^2=x^2\Rightarrow x^2\left(1-y^2\right)=y^2 \Rightarrow x=\sqrt{\frac{y^2}{1-y^2}}\Rightarrow \frac{y^2}{1-y^2} \geq 0$ $\therefore y \in(-1,1)$ So, $f(x)$ is not surjective.

The given equations are
$3 l+m+5 n=0$  ...(i)
and $6 \mathrm{mn}-2 \mathrm{n} l+5 l \mathrm{m}=0$  ...(ii)

If $l=-2 \mathrm{n}$, then putting $l=-2 \mathrm{n}$ in (i), we obtain $\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{n}$.
Thus, the direction ratios of two lines are $-\mathrm{n},-2 \mathrm{n}, \mathrm{n}$ and $-2 \mathrm{n}, \mathrm{n}, \mathrm{n}$ i.e., $1,2,-1$ and $-2,1,1$.

& \Rightarrow \theta=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{-1}{6}\right)

questions.solution: Energy is, $\mathrm{E}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\mathrm{E}=\frac{1242 \mathrm{~nm}-\mathrm{eV}}{\lambda} \Rightarrow \lambda=\frac{1242}{6}=207 \mathrm{~nm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: There are two long co-axial solenoids of same length $l$. The inner and outer coils have radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ and number of turns per unit length $n_1$ and $n_2$, respectively. The ratio of mutual inductance to the self-inductance of the inner-coil is:
questions.solution:
The rate of mutual inductance is given by
$\mathrm{M}=\mu_0 \mathrm{n}_1 \mathrm{n}_2 \pi \mathrm{~m}_1^2$  ....(i)
The rate of self inductance is given by
$\mathrm{L}=\mu_0 \mathrm{n}_1^2 \pi \mathrm{r}_1^2$  .....(ii)
Dividing (i) by (ii)
$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{M}}{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_2}{\mathrm{n}_1}$

questions.q:
Electric potential at a point 'P' due to a point charge of $5 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{C}$ is 50 V . The distance of ' P ' from the point charge is:
(Assume, $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}=9 \times 10^{+9} \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrm{C}^{-2}$ )
questions.solution: Electric potential at a point P due to a point charge, $\left(\because \mathrm{K}=9 \times 10^9\right)V_P=\frac{K Q}{r}\Rightarrow \quad 50=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 5 \times 10^{-9}}{\mathrm{r}}\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{r}=\frac{45}{50}=\frac{9}{10}=0.9 \mathrm{~m}=90 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: One main scale division of a vernier caliper is equal to $m$ units. If ${m}^{\text {th }}$ division of main scale coincides with $(n+1)^{\text {th }}$ division of vernier scale, the least count of the vernier caliper is:
questions.solution:
Given 1 Main scale division = m
$\mathrm{n} M S D=(\mathrm{n}+1) \mathrm{VSD}\Rightarrow \quad 1 \mathrm{VSD}=\frac{\mathrm{n}}{\mathrm{n}+1} \mathrm{MSD}$
Least count of vernier caliper $=1 \mathrm{MSD}-1 \mathrm{VSD}\Rightarrow \quad L . C=m-m\left(\frac{n}{n+1}\right)=\left(1-\frac{n}{n+1}\right) m=m\left(\frac{n+1-n}{n+1}\right)=\left(\frac{1}{n+1}\right) m \Rightarrow L \cdot C=\left(\frac{m}{n+1}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance between Sun and Earth is $R$. The duration of year if the distance between Sun and Earth becomes $3 R$ will be:
questions.solution:
Basically 1 year is equal to time period of earth revolution around sun.
So, $T_i=1$ year
Now,
$T^2 \propto R^3\therefore\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^2=\left(\frac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^3\Rightarrow T_2=\left(\frac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^{3 / 2} T_1=\left(\frac{3 R}{R}\right)^{3 / 2} \times 1=3 \sqrt{3}$ years.

questions.q: The temperature of an ideal gas is increased from 200 K to 800 K . If r.m.s. speed of gas at 200 K is $v_0$. Then, r.m.s. speed of the gas at 800 K will be:
questions.solution:
RMS speed,
$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{mm}} \propto \sqrt{\mathrm{T}}$
Here, $\mathrm{T}_{\text {initiol }}=200 \mathrm{~K}\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{fing1}}=800 \mathrm{~K}$
Initial RMS speed $=\mathrm{v}_0\therefore \frac{v_0}{v_{\mathrm{rms}}}=\sqrt{\frac{200}{800}} \Rightarrow v_{\mathrm{ms}}=2 v_0$

questions.q: A light string passing over a smooth light pulley connects two blocks of masses $\mathrm{m}_1$ and $\mathrm{m}_2$ (where $m_2 \gt m_1$). If the acceleration of the system is $\frac{\mathrm{g}}{\sqrt{2}}$, then the ratio of the masses $\frac{m_1}{m_2}$ is:
questions.solution:
Acceleration is given as:
$a=\left(\frac{m_2-m_1}{m_1+m_2}\right) g\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{g}}{\sqrt{2}}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{m}_2-\mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{~m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2}\right) \mathrm{g}\Rightarrow \sqrt{2}\left(m_2-m_1\right)=m_1+m_2\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{m}_1}{\mathrm{~m}_2}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1}\right)$

When the block is pushed up by 10 m along inclined surface, the work done against frictional force is : $\left[g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right]$

questions.q: A long straight wire of radius a carries a steady current 1 . The current is uniformly distributed across its cross section. The ratio of the magnetic field at $\frac{\mathrm{a}}{2}$ and 2a from axis of the wire is:

Magnetic field due to straight wire,

questions.q: Pressure inside two soap bubbles are 1.01 and 1.02 atmosphere, respectively. The ratio of their volumes is :
questions.solution:
According to question, pressure inside, 1st soap bubble,
$\Delta P_1=P_1-P_0=0.01=\frac{4 T}{R_1}$  .....(i)
And $\Delta P_2=P_2-P_0=0.02=\frac{4 T}{R_2}$  .....(ii)
Dividing, equation (ii) by (i),
$\frac{1}{2}=\frac{R_2}{R_1} \Rightarrow R_1=2 R_2$
Volume $V=\frac{4}{3} \pi R^3 \Rightarrow \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\frac{R_1^3}{R_2^3}=\frac{8 R_2^3}{R_2^3}=\frac{8}{1}$

Young's modulus, $\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\text { Stress }}{\text { Strain }}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A particle is moving in a straight line. The variation of position ' $x$ ' as a function of time ' $t$ ' is given as $x=\left(t^3-6 t^2+20 t+15\right) m$.
The velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero is:
questions.solution:
Displacement, $x=t^3-6 t^2+20 t+15\therefore$ Velocity, $v=\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=3 \mathrm{t}^2-12 \mathrm{t}+20\therefore$ Acceleration, $a=\frac{d v}{d t}=6 t-12$
When $a=0\Rightarrow 6 \mathrm{t}-12=0 \Rightarrow t=2 \mathrm{~s}$
At $\mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~s}, v=3(2)^2-12(2)+20=8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.q: The range of the projectile projected at an angle of $15^{\circ}$ with horizontal is 50 m . If the projectile is projected with same velocity at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with horizontal, then its range will be :
questions.solution:
Range of projectile
$R=\frac{v^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}(\because R \propto \sin (2 \theta))\frac{R_1}{R_2}=\frac{\sin \left(2 \theta_1\right)}{\sin \left(2 \theta_2\right)}=\frac{\sin (2 \times 15)}{\sin (2 \times 45)}=\frac{\sin 30^{\circ}}{\sin 90^{\circ}}\Rightarrow \frac{50}{\mathrm{R}_2}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_2=100 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with a velocity ' $u$ ' making an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. The magnitude of angular momentum of the projectile about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height $h$ is:

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between $x=-A$ and $x=+A$. If time taken by particle to go from $x=0$ to $\frac{A}{2}$ is $2 s$; then time taken by particle in going from $x=\frac{A}{2}$ to $A$ is:
questions.solution: Let time from 0 to $\mathrm{A} / 2$ is $\mathrm{t}_1$ and from $\mathrm{A} / 2$ to A is $\mathrm{t}_2$ From the standard equation of SHM, $\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{A}}{2}=\mathrm{A} \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}_1\right)\Rightarrow \omega t_1=\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$ ....(i) Using $x=A_0 \sin \omega t$ again $A=A \sin \omega\left(t_1+t_2\right)\omega\left(t_1+t_2\right)=\sin ^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}$ Using (i) $\omega t_2=\frac{\pi}{2}-\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}$ .....(ii) Dividing equation (i) by (ii) we get $\frac{t_1}{t_2}=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow \quad t_2=2 t_1=2 \times 2=4 \mathrm{sec}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A solid metallic cube having total surface area $24 \mathrm{~m}^2$ is uniformly heated. If its temperature is increased by $10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, calculate the increase in volume of the cube.
$\left(\right.$ Given : $\left.\alpha=5.0 \times 10^{-4}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}\right)$
questions.solution:
We have $\Delta V=V_0 \gamma \Delta T\Delta V=a^3,(3 \alpha) \Delta T$
Now, $6 a^2=24 \quad[\because$ Total surface area of cube $\left.=6 a^2\right]\Rightarrow a^2=4 \Rightarrow a=2$
So, $\Delta V=2^3\left(3 \times 5 \times 10^{-4}\right) \times 10=1200 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^3=1200 \times 10^2 \mathrm{~cm}^3=1.2 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~cm}^3$

questions.q: A gas can be taken from A to B via two different processes $A C B$ and $A D B$. When path $A C B$ is used 60 J of heat flows into the system and 30J of work is done by the system. If path ADB is used work done by the system is 10 J . The heat Flow into the system in path ADB is :
questions.solution: $\triangle \mathrm{U}$ remains same for both paths ACB and ADB $\Delta Q_{A C B}=\Delta W_{A C B}+\Delta U_{A C B}$ $\Rightarrow 60 \mathrm{~J}=30 \mathrm{~J}+\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{ACB}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{ACB}}=30 \mathrm{~J}$ As change in internal energy depends only on initial and final point $\therefore \Delta \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{ADB}}=\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{ACB}}=30 \mathrm{~J}\Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{ADB}}=\Delta \mathrm{U}_{\mathrm{ADB}}+\Delta \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{ADB}}=10 \mathrm{~J}+30 \mathrm{~J}=40 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The speed of sound in oxygen at S.T.P. will be approximately:
(Given, $\left.\mathrm{R}=8.3 \mathrm{JK}^{-1}, \gamma=1.4\right)$
questions.solution:
At STP
Temperature, $T=273 \mathrm{~K}$
Molecular mass of oxygen, $\mathrm{M}=32 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~kg}$
Speed of sound is given by
$\mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma \mathrm{RT}}{\mathrm{M}}}=\sqrt{\frac{1.4 \times 8.3 \times 273}{32 \times 10^{-3}}}=314.8541 \simeq 315 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$
